spec.description: Trade a refresh token for a fresh session. The core does this on its own when an access token expires mid-call, retries the call once, and only then gives up.

request.title: RefreshSessionRequest
request.description: Takes nothing. The refresh token travels as the bearer, in place of the access token -- which is the whole reason this endpoint declares `inject: refresh` rather than being an ordinary authenticated call.

response.title: Session
response.description: A session: two tokens and who they belong to.

accessJwt.description: Bearer token for authenticated calls. Short-lived -- minutes, not days -- so a long-running client refreshes rather than reusing it.

refreshJwt.description: Token that buys a new `accessJwt` from `server.refresh_session`. Longer-lived, and the more dangerous of the two to leak.

handle.description: Handle the session belongs to, such as `truewire.dev`.

active.description: Whether the account is active. A deactivated or taken-down account still authenticates and answers `false` here.

email.description: Account email. Present on `createSession` and absent from `refreshSession`; it is personal data, so recorded examples scrub it.

emailConfirmed.description: Whether that address has been confirmed.
